# Try it: drag and drop a profile

Drop one or more plot-data JSON files below and see them rendered, without
installing anything or writing any code. This page runs entirely in your
browser -- files you drop here are never uploaded anywhere.

Export the files with:

```sh
scope-profiler export plot-data run*.h5 -o figures --format json --with
```

Then drag `figures/*.json` (or a single file) onto the box below. Each file
gets its own figure, in the order you dropped them; `region_statistics.json`
renders as a summary table instead of a chart.

```{=html}
<div id="scope-plotly-dropzone"
     style="border: 2px dashed var(--color-foreground-border, #999); border-radius: 8px; padding: 2.5rem 1rem; text-align: center; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 0.15s, background-color 0.15s;">
  <p style="margin: 0;">Drop plot-data <code>.json</code> files here, or click to choose</p>
  <input id="scope-plotly-dropzone-input" type="file" accept="application/json,.json" multiple style="display: none;" />
</div>
<div id="scope-plotly-dropzone-errors" style="margin-top: 0.75rem; color: #c0392b;"></div>
<div id="scope-plotly-dropzone-figures" style="display: grid; gap: 1.5rem; margin: 1.5rem 0;"></div>
<script src="https://cdn.plot.ly/plotly-3.7.0.min.js"></script>
<script type="module">
  const { buildFigure, renderFigure } = await import("../_static/plotly/index.js");
  const zone = document.getElementById("scope-plotly-dropzone");
  const input = document.getElementById("scope-plotly-dropzone-input");
  const errors = document.getElementById("scope-plotly-dropzone-errors");
  const figures = document.getElementById("scope-plotly-dropzone-figures");
  const setActive = (active) => {
    zone.style.borderColor = active ? "#2a78d6" : "";
    zone.style.backgroundColor = active ? "rgba(42, 120, 214, 0.08)" : "";
  };
  async function handleFiles(fileList) {
    errors.textContent = "";
    for (const file of fileList) {
      const card = document.createElement("div");
      const title = document.createElement("strong");
      title.textContent = file.name;
      const plot = document.createElement("div");
      plot.style.minHeight = "360px";
      card.append(title, plot);
      figures.append(card);
      try {
        const payload = JSON.parse(await file.text());
        const figure = buildFigure(payload);
        await renderFigure(window.Plotly, plot, figure);
      } catch (error) {
        card.remove();
        const message = document.createElement("p");
        message.textContent = `${file.name}: ${error.message}`;
        errors.append(message);
      }
    }
  }
  zone.addEventListener("click", () => input.click());
  input.addEventListener("change", () => handleFiles(input.files));
  for (const event of ["dragenter", "dragover"]) {
    zone.addEventListener(event, (e) => {
      e.preventDefault();
      setActive(true);
    });
  }
  for (const event of ["dragleave", "drop"]) {
    zone.addEventListener(event, (e) => {
      e.preventDefault();
      setActive(false);
    });
  }
  zone.addEventListener("drop", (e) => handleFiles(e.dataTransfer.files));
</script>
```

## Under the hood

This is the same recipe as {doc}`dashboard`, minus the build step: `buildFigure`
reads the `plot` field each exported JSON file carries and dispatches to the
matching builder, so one drop zone handles every plot kind without naming any
of them. Nothing here needs a server -- the same `<div>` and `<script type="module">`
work in a plain `index.html` served from a bucket, which is the point of
shipping `@scope-profiler/plotly` as a dependency-free package in the first
place.

For a page that keeps several figures in sync with a theme toggle or a filter
box across repeated renders, see {doc}`dashboard`.
